I am a 42-year-old farmer in Afar with no schooling, and my family depends on this 0.81-hectare sorghum plot and our livestock. The rains here are unpredictable and often too little, so I will not risk scarce money on chemical fertilizer that the cooperative might not even deliver on time, and I do not trust these new seeds. I will spread whatever goat and cattle manure I can collect from our animals onto the field, as my father taught me, and we will do all the work ourselves—ploughing with oxen, weeding by hand, and harvesting when the heads are dry.
